title: Network policies
summary: By default every pod can talk to every pod. Change that.

steps.title: Default allow, then isolate
body: Out of the box the pod network is flat: any pod can reach any pod in any namespace. A **NetworkPolicy** selects pods and, once a pod is selected by any policy for a direction (ingress or egress), **only traffic some policy allows** gets through in that direction.
podSelector: { matchLabels: { app: postgres } }   # protects these pods
Result: postgres pods accept TCP 5432 from `shop-api` pods in `shop`, and nothing else. Pods no policy selects are unaffected.
> **Tip:** Policies are enforced by the network plugin (Calico, Cilium, Azure NPM...). On a cluster whose CNI does not support them, they are accepted and **silently ignored**.
A common baseline is a **default deny** per namespace (`podSelector: {}` with no ingress rules) and then explicit allows.

steps.prompt: Only policy in namespace `shop`: the one on the card. Which connections succeed? (Postgres listens on 5432.)
items: postgres pod to a `shop-api` pod on 8080 (no policy selects shop-api)
steps.explain: A bare `podSelector` in `from` only means pods in the policy's own namespace. Use `namespaceSelector` to allow other namespaces. Policies select the *destination* for ingress; the shop-api pods themselves are not restricted.

steps.prompt: You add a default-deny ingress policy to namespace `shop`. Suddenly the ingress controller (in namespace `ingress-nginx`) gets 504s for every site. Why?
options: The controller's traffic into `shop` pods is now denied; you must allow it with a `namespaceSelector` for `ingress-nginx`
Default deny also blocks DNS for the controller
steps.explain: Default deny means *everything* into those pods, including from the ingress controller and from Prometheus scraping metrics.

steps.prompt: Allow traffic into the selected pods from any pod in namespaces labelled `team=frontend`.
Egress default-deny breaks every outbound HTTP call **by name**, even to allowed IPs. What did you forget to allow?
options: UDP and TCP port 53 to the cluster DNS (kube-dns / CoreDNS) pods
steps.explain: Name resolution happens first. Every egress-deny setup needs an explicit DNS allow.

steps.prompt: Ingress isolation in one line. A pod is selected by no policy. What does this print?
steps.explain: Unselected pods stay wide open. Isolation only starts when a policy selects the pod.

steps.prompt: You apply a NetworkPolicy on a kind cluster using its default CNI, and traffic is not blocked at all. Why?
options: The network plugin does not enforce NetworkPolicy, so the object is stored but ignored
Policies take an hour to apply
kind clusters have no pod network
Policies only work on LoadBalancer Services
steps.explain: Install a CNI that enforces policies (Calico, Cilium) when you need to test them locally. Always test that a deny actually denies.

steps.title: Evaluate ingress policies
prompt: Model ingress policies within one namespace. Each policy has a pod selector (`Target`) and a list of allowed sources, each `(Dictionary<string,string> From, int Port)`.

Write `bool Allowed(Dictionary<string, string> src, Dictionary<string, string> dst, int port, List<(Dictionary<string, string> Target, List<(Dictionary<string, string> From, int Port)> Rules)> policies)`:
- if no policy's `Target` matches `dst`, the connection is allowed
- otherwise it is allowed only if some **selecting** policy has a rule whose `From` matches `src` and whose `Port` equals `port` (`Port` 0 means any port)
starter: bool Allowed(Dictionary<string, string> src, Dictionary<string, string> dst, int port, List<(Dictionary<string, string> Target, List<(Dictionary<string, string> From, int Port)> Rules)> policies)
solution: bool M(Dictionary<string, string> sel, Dictionary<string, string> labels) =>
sel.All(kv => labels.TryGetValue(kv.Key, out var v) && v == kv.Value);
bool Allowed(Dictionary<string, string> src, Dictionary<string, string> dst, int port, List<(Dictionary<string, string> Target, List<(Dictionary<string, string> From, int Port)> Rules)> policies)
return selecting.Any(p => p.Rules.Any(r => M(r.From, src) && (r.Port == 0 || r.Port == port)));
template: var dojoPol = new List<(Dictionary<string, string> Target, List<(Dictionary<string, string> From, int Port)> Rules)> {
Dojo.Check("api -> db:5432 allowed", Allowed(dojoApi, dojoDb, 5432, dojoPol), "");
Dojo.Check("web -> api allowed (api not selected)", Allowed(dojoWeb, dojoApi, 8080, dojoPol), "");
var dojoDeny = new List<(Dictionary<string, string> Target, List<(Dictionary<string, string> From, int Port)> Rules)> {
Dojo.Check("default deny: web -> db denied", !Allowed(dojoWeb, dojoDb, 5432, dojoDeny), "");
Dojo.Check("default deny + allow: web -> api any port", Allowed(dojoWeb, dojoApi, 9999, dojoDeny), "");
Dojo.Check("default deny: db -> web denied", !Allowed(dojoDb, dojoWeb, 80, dojoDeny), "");
hints: First find the policies that select `dst`. None? Allowed.
Then `Any` policy with `Any` rule matching source and port.
